compatibility_conditions.reason: Task specifies 45 degree incidence; design must account for angular shift.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same material order, substrate, incident medium, 45-degree unpolarized illumination.
expectations.reason: Increasing thickness shifts the Bragg condition to longer wavelengths; if the baseline is too blue-shifted at 45 degrees, thicker layers may better center the stopband on the visible region.

expectations.controlled_conditions: Same material order, substrate, incident medium, 45-degree unpolarized illumination.

jobs.rationale: Hypothesis: The catastrophic G2 loss in P075 is driven by excessive reflection from the deepest high-index layers (L10) and the interface layer (L0). This branch tests a 'front-loaded' strategy: slightly thickening L0 and L2 to sharpen the visible band edge while thinning L10 to reduce NIR leakage, aiming to recover G2 without sacrificing the G1 gains.

route.claim: A model-knowledge hypothesis that matching the optical phase thickness of s and p polarizations via specific non-quarter-wave ratios reduces polarization leakage.
transfer_assumptions: At 45 degrees, s and p waves see different effective indices. Standard quarter-wave layers are not optimal for both simultaneously.
Adjusting thickness ratios can align the reflection phases for both polarizations.

compatibility_conditions.reason: Task requires equal-s/p average; minimizing split improves the mean.

expectations.reason: Hypothesis: Adjusting the ratio moves the s and p reflection bands closer together, reducing the 'dip' in the unpolarized average caused by polarization splitting.

route.model_knowledge_rationale: Based on Fresnel equations, s and p admittances diverge at oblique angles. A quarter-wave stack optimized for normal incidence splits into two distinct bands at 45 degrees. By empirically tuning thicknesses (thickening H, thinning L or vice versa), one can attempt to overlap these bands or create a composite plateau that maximizes the unpolarized mean.
